decks.title: Mineral Resources — Part 1: Iron ore and manganese
goals: Name the types of iron ore and state uses of iron
Name two leading iron-ore producing states and a prominent mining area in each
State the uses of manganese and name two leading states with their mining areas

slides.heading: Metals that build a nation
slides.body_md: Part 1 — rails, bridges, buses and pressure cookers all begin as rock dug from the hills of Odisha, Chhattisgarh and Jharkhand. This chapter studies four metallic minerals: **iron ore**, **manganese**, **copper** and **bauxite**.

visual.alt: Table of the four minerals in this chapter with type and main use

slides.narration: Namaste! Railway lines, bridges, buses and even the pressure cooker in your kitchen began as rock dug out of the hills of eastern and central India. In this chapter we study four metallic minerals. Iron ore and manganese are ferrous minerals, used for iron and steel. Copper and bauxite are non ferrous. Let us start with iron ore and manganese.

slides.heading: Minerals, ores and their grade
slides.body_md: A **mineral** is a naturally occurring substance with a definite chemical composition. An **ore** is a mineral or rock from which a metal can be extracted **profitably**. The **grade** of an ore is the share of metal in it: a high-grade ore gives more metal per tonne and less waste. **Ferrous** minerals contain iron or are used with it (iron ore, manganese); **non-ferrous** metallic minerals do not (copper, bauxite).

rows: Rock from which a metal is extracted profitably
Share of metal in the ore

visual.alt: Table of terms used for minerals and ores with examples

slides.narration: A mineral is a natural substance with a fixed chemical make up. When a metal can be taken out of a rock at a profit, we call that rock an ore. The grade of an ore tells us how much metal it contains: the higher the grade, the more metal and the less waste. Iron ore and manganese are ferrous minerals; copper and bauxite are non ferrous.

slides.heading: Types of iron ore
slides.body_md: **Magnetite:** black, **magnetic**, the **richest** ore (up to about 70% iron). **Hematite:** **reddish**, about 60–70% iron; it is the ore **most mined in India** and feeds most of our steel plants. **Limonite:** **yellowish-brown**, contains water, lower grade (roughly 35–50%). **Siderite:** a **carbonate** of iron with many impurities and a low iron content. Approximate values; grades vary from deposit to deposit.

slides.narration: There are four main iron ores. Magnetite is black and magnetic, and it is the richest. Hematite is reddish and also rich, and it is the ore mined most in India. Limonite is yellowish brown, holds water in its structure and is of lower grade. Siderite is a carbonate of iron with many impurities and the least iron of the four.

slides.heading: Quick check: types of iron ore
slides.body_md: Identify an iron ore from its description.
slides.narration: Quick check. Magnetite is black and magnetic, hematite reddish, limonite yellowish brown, siderite a carbonate.

slides.heading: Uses of iron
slides.body_md: Iron is the **basic metal of modern industry**. Iron ore is smelted with **coke** (from coking coal) and **limestone** in a **blast furnace** to make **pig iron**, which is refined into **steel**. Steel is used for **railways, bridges, ships, buildings, machinery, vehicles, tools, pipes, utensils** and defence equipment. Because almost every other industry needs iron and steel, iron ore is called the **backbone** of industrial development.

visual.alt: Flow from iron ore, coke and limestone through the blast furnace to pig iron, steel and finished goods

slides.narration: Iron ore is melted with coke and limestone in a blast furnace to make pig iron, which is then refined into steel. Steel goes into railway lines, bridges, ships, buildings, machines, cars, tools and kitchen utensils. Since nearly every other industry needs iron and steel, iron ore is often called the backbone of industry.

slides.heading: Distribution of iron ore
slides.body_md: India has large reserves of high-grade **hematite** and **magnetite**. **Leading states (as of the early 2020s): Odisha and Chhattisgarh**, followed by **Karnataka** and **Jharkhand**. **Odisha:** **Keonjhar** (Joda, Barbil), **Sundargarh** (Bonai) and **Mayurbhanj** (Gorumahisani, Badampahar, Sulaipat). **Chhattisgarh:** **Bailadila** range in Dantewada (very high-grade hematite) and **Dalli-Rajhara** in Balod–Durg (feeds the Bhilai steel plant). **Jharkhand:** **Noamundi** and Gua in Singhbhum. **Karnataka:** **Bellary–Hospet** (Sandur).

visual.alt: Table of iron-ore producing states and their mining areas

slides.narration: Most of India’s iron ore comes from the old rocks of the eastern and central plateau. Odisha and Chhattisgarh are the leading producers. In Odisha the main mines are in Keonjhar, Sundargarh and Mayurbhanj districts. In Chhattisgarh, the Bailadila hills give very rich hematite, and the Dalli Rajhara mines supply the Bhilai steel plant. Jharkhand and Karnataka are also important.

slides.heading: How iron ore is mined: open-cast mining
slides.body_md: Much of India’s iron ore lies in **thick deposits near the surface** of hill ranges such as Bailadila and the Keonjhar hills, so it is mined by **open-cast (open-pit) methods**: the **overburden** of soil and waste rock is removed and the ore is cut in **benches** (steps) by machines, then carried away by trucks, conveyors and railways. Open-cast mining is cheaper and safer than underground mining but scars the land, so pits must later be **reclaimed** and replanted.

slides.narration: Iron ore in India often lies in thick layers close to the surface, on the tops of hills. So it is mined in open pits. First the soil and waste rock on top, called overburden, is removed. Then machines cut the ore in a series of steps called benches, and trucks carry it out. This is cheaper and safer than tunnelling, but the land must be repaired afterwards.

slides.heading: Worked example: why steel plants stand near iron-ore mines
slides.body_md:
**Problem.** Explain why the Bhilai steel plant was built in Chhattisgarh and the Rourkela plant in Odisha.

**Step 1. Bulky raw material.** Several tonnes of raw materials go into each tonne of steel, and iron ore is the heaviest; carrying it far is costly, so plants are built near the ore (Dalli-Rajhara for Bhilai; Keonjhar–Sundargarh for Rourkela).

**Step 2. Other inputs nearby.** Coal from the Jharkhand–Chhattisgarh–Odisha fields, limestone, manganese and dolomite are found in the same region.

**Step 3. Transport and water.** Railway lines link mines and plants; rivers supply water for cooling.

visual.alt: Flow of three reasons leading steel plants to locate near iron-ore mines

slides.narration: Why are Bhilai and Rourkela where they are? Steel needs several tonnes of raw material for every tonne of product, and iron ore is the heaviest part, so it is cheaper to build the plant near the mines. Coal, limestone and manganese are also found in the same region. Railways connect the mines to the plants, and nearby rivers provide water.

slides.heading: Quick check: iron-ore areas
slides.body_md: Link a mining area to iron ore and its state.
slides.narration: Quick check. Keonjhar and Bailadila are rich iron ore areas of Odisha and Chhattisgarh.

slides.heading: Manganese: uses and distribution
slides.body_md: **Uses:** mainly in the **iron and steel industry** — as **ferro-manganese**, an alloy that **hardens steel** and **removes impurities** such as sulphur and oxygen; also in **dry-cell batteries**, **bleaching powder**, **insecticides**, **paints**, glass and ceramics. **Distribution:** leading states **(as of the early 2020s)** include **Madhya Pradesh**, **Maharashtra** and **Odisha**, with Karnataka. **Madhya Pradesh:** **Balaghat** and **Chhindwara**. **Maharashtra:** **Nagpur** and **Bhandara**. **Odisha:** **Keonjhar**, **Sundargarh** and **Koraput**. **Karnataka:** **Sandur** (Bellary).

visual.alt: Table of manganese-producing states and their mining areas

slides.narration: Manganese is mostly used in making steel. Mixed with iron as ferro manganese, it makes steel hard and tough and removes harmful impurities. It is also used in batteries, bleaching powder, paints and insecticides. Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra and Odisha are leading producers. The main areas are Balaghat and Chhindwara in Madhya Pradesh, Nagpur and Bhandara in Maharashtra, and Keonjhar and Sundargarh in Odisha.

slides.heading: Worked example: grade and tonnage
slides.body_md:
**Problem.** Using the illustrative grades (hematite 65%, limonite 45%), how much iron is contained in 1000 t of each ore? How much limonite would be needed to give as much iron as 1000 t of hematite?

**Step 1.** Hematite: $\frac{65}{100} \times 1000 = 650$ t of iron.

**Step 2.** Limonite: $\frac{45}{100} \times 1000 = 450$ t of iron.

**Step 3.** Limonite needed $= \frac{650}{0.45} = 1444.4$ t (rounded).

**Interpret.** A low-grade ore means far more rock to mine, carry and smelt for the same iron — one reason high-grade hematite is prized.

visual.alt: Table of illustrative iron content in a thousand tonnes of hematite and of limonite

slides.narration: Let us compare two ores. A thousand tonnes of hematite at sixty five per cent iron contains six hundred and fifty tonnes of iron. The same weight of limonite at forty five per cent contains only four hundred and fifty tonnes. To get six hundred and fifty tonnes of iron from limonite, we would need about one thousand four hundred and forty four tonnes of rock. Grade really matters.

slides.heading: Quick check: manganese
slides.body_md: State a use of manganese or name a manganese area.
slides.narration: Quick check. Manganese hardens steel; Balaghat and Nagpur are manganese areas.

slides.heading: Summary: Part 1
bullets: Iron ores: magnetite (richest, magnetic), hematite (most mined in India), limonite (yellow-brown, hydrated), siderite (carbonate, low grade).
Uses of iron: steel for railways, bridges, ships, machinery, vehicles, buildings, tools.
Leading iron-ore states: Odisha (Keonjhar, Sundargarh, Mayurbhanj) and Chhattisgarh (Bailadila, Dalli-Rajhara); also Jharkhand (Noamundi) and Karnataka (Bellary–Hospet).
Manganese: hardens steel (ferro-manganese), batteries, bleaching powder, paints; Madhya Pradesh (Balaghat), Maharashtra (Nagpur), Odisha (Keonjhar).

visual.alt: Summary table of leading states and areas for iron ore and manganese

slides.narration: Let us sum up Part 1. The four iron ores are magnetite, hematite, limonite and siderite, and hematite is the one mined most in India. Iron is turned into steel for almost everything. Odisha and Chhattisgarh lead in iron ore. Manganese hardens steel and is used in batteries and bleaching powder; Balaghat, Nagpur and Keonjhar are important manganese areas.

slides.heading: Exam tips: Part 1
bullets: Learn the four iron ores in order of iron content.
For distribution, always pair a state with a named mining area.
Give at least two uses for each mineral, not just "industry".
Mark ranks with care: production ranks can change from year to year.

visual.alt: Table of three common slips in Part 1 and their fixes

slides.narration: Some tips. Remember the four iron ores in order of iron content. Whenever you name a state, add a mining area. Give at least two specific uses for each mineral. And be careful with rankings of producing states, because these can change from year to year.

decks.title: Mineral Resources — Part 2: Copper and bauxite
goals: State the uses of copper and name two leading states with their mining areas
State the uses of bauxite and name two leading states with their mining areas
Follow the journey from ore to metal and work with ore grades

slides.heading: Wires and wings
slides.body_md: Part 2 — the wiring in your home is probably copper; the overhead power line outside and the body of an aeroplane are largely aluminium, made from **bauxite**. Both are **non-ferrous** metals.

visual.alt: Table of copper and bauxite with their metals, properties and uses

slides.narration: Look around you. The wires inside the walls are probably copper. The power lines on tall towers and the body of an aeroplane are mostly aluminium, which is made from bauxite. Copper and aluminium are non ferrous metals: they contain no iron. In this part we study where their ores are found and what they are used for.

slides.heading: Copper: uses
slides.body_md: Copper is an **excellent conductor** of electricity and heat, is **ductile** (can be drawn into thin wires) and **malleable**, and resists corrosion. **Uses:** **electrical cables and wires**, **motors, transformers and generators**, **electronics** and telephone cables, **utensils** and heat exchangers, coins, and alloys: **brass** (copper + zinc) for fittings and decorative ware; **bronze** (copper + tin) for statues, bells and bearings.

visual.alt: Flow showing copper used pure for wires and alloyed into brass and bronze

slides.narration: Copper carries electricity and heat extremely well, can be drawn into fine wires and does not rust. So it is used for electrical wiring, motors, transformers and electronic goods, as well as for utensils. Mixed with zinc it makes brass, used for taps and fittings. Mixed with tin it makes bronze, used for statues and bells, like the famous bronzes of Thanjavur.

slides.heading: Copper: distribution
slides.body_md: India has **limited reserves** of copper, mostly of **low grade**, and **imports** much of what it uses. **Leading states (as of the early 2020s): Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan**, with **Jharkhand**. **Madhya Pradesh:** **Malanjkhand** in **Balaghat** district, a large open-cast mine. **Rajasthan:** **Khetri–Singhana** in **Jhunjhunu** district (Khetri copper complex), also Alwar. **Jharkhand:** the **Singhbhum** copper belt (**Ghatsila, Mosabani, Rakha**).

visual.alt: Table of copper-producing states and their mining areas

slides.narration: India does not have much copper, and most of its ore is of low grade, so the country imports a lot. The leading copper states are Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan, with Jharkhand. Malanjkhand in Balaghat district of Madhya Pradesh is a large open pit mine. Khetri in Jhunjhunu district of Rajasthan is a famous copper complex. In Jharkhand, the Singhbhum belt has mines at Ghatsila and Mosabani.

slides.heading: Quick check: copper
slides.body_md: Name a copper alloy or a copper-mining area.
slides.narration: Quick check. Brass is copper with zinc; bronze is copper with tin; Malanjkhand and Khetri are copper mines.

slides.heading: Worked example: why so much rock for so little copper
slides.body_md:
**Problem.** An Indian copper ore contains about 1.2% copper (illustrative). How much copper can be obtained from 40000 t of ore, and what does this tell us?

**Step 1.** Copper $= \frac{1.2}{100} \times 40000 = 480$ t.

**Step 2.** Waste rock $= 40000 - 480 = 39520$ t.

**Interpret.** Almost all the rock is waste, so mining, crushing and concentrating copper is costly and produces huge heaps of tailings. With limited, low-grade ore and rising demand for wires and electronics, India must **import** much of its copper.

visual.alt: Table of illustrative ore mined, copper obtained and waste rock

slides.narration: Suppose our copper ore contains a little over one per cent copper. From forty thousand tonnes of ore we get only about four hundred and eighty tonnes of copper; everything else is waste rock. That makes copper expensive to produce. Since our deposits are small and of low grade, while demand for wires and electronics keeps growing, India has to import much of its copper.

slides.heading: Bauxite: uses
slides.body_md: **Bauxite** is the **ore of aluminium** — a clay-like rock rich in hydrated aluminium oxide. Aluminium is **light, strong, a good conductor**, **does not rust** and can be rolled thin. **Uses of aluminium:** **aircraft** and vehicles, **overhead electric cables**, **utensils**, **packaging** (foil, cans), window frames and building panels. **Bauxite** itself is also used in making **cement**, **abrasives** and heat-resistant **refractory** bricks.

visual.alt: Table linking properties of aluminium to its uses

slides.narration: Bauxite is the ore from which aluminium is made. Aluminium is light but strong, carries electricity well, does not rust and can be rolled into thin foil. So it is used to build aircraft and vehicles, to make overhead power cables, cooking utensils, food foil and drink cans, and window frames. Bauxite itself is also used in cement and heat resistant bricks.

slides.heading: From bauxite to aluminium
slides.body_md: Bauxite is mined, then **refined** into a white powder, **alumina** (aluminium oxide), at a **refinery** — for example at **Damanjodi** in Odisha, near the Koraput mines. Alumina is then **smelted** by electrolysis into **aluminium** at a **smelter** such as **Angul** or **Hirakud** in Odisha or **Renukoot** in Uttar Pradesh. Smelting uses **huge amounts of electricity**, so smelters are sited near **cheap power**. Rounded illustrative ratio: about 5 t bauxite → 2 t alumina → 1 t aluminium.

slides.narration: Bauxite goes on a journey. First it is refined into a white powder called alumina, at a refinery near the mines, such as Damanjodi in Odisha. Then the alumina is split into aluminium using a great deal of electricity, at a smelter such as Angul, Hirakud or Renukoot. Roughly five tonnes of bauxite give two tonnes of alumina and finally one tonne of aluminium.

slides.heading: Quick check: bauxite and aluminium
slides.body_md: Explain a step from bauxite to aluminium.
slides.narration: Quick check. Bauxite is refined to alumina, then smelted to aluminium using much electricity.

slides.heading: Bauxite: distribution
slides.body_md: Bauxite forms in **laterite** areas of the plateaus and hills. **Leading states (as of the early 2020s): Odisha** (by far the largest) and **Gujarat**, with **Jharkhand**, **Chhattisgarh**, **Maharashtra** and **Madhya Pradesh**. **Odisha:** **Koraput** (Panchpatmali hills) and **Kalahandi**. **Gujarat:** **Jamnagar**, **Kutch** and **Bhavnagar** (Saurashtra). **Jharkhand:** **Lohardaga**. **Chhattisgarh:** **Mainpat** plateau (Surguja) and the **Amarkantak** plateau. **Maharashtra:** **Kolhapur** and **Ratnagiri**.

visual.alt: Table of bauxite-producing states and their mining areas

slides.narration: Bauxite is found on the laterite capped plateaus and hills of India. Odisha is by far the largest producer, from Koraput and Kalahandi districts. Gujarat is another leading state, with deposits in Jamnagar and Kutch. Lohardaga in Jharkhand, the Mainpat and Amarkantak plateaus in Chhattisgarh, and Kolhapur in Maharashtra are other important areas.

slides.heading: Worked example: supplying a smelter
slides.body_md:
**Problem.** A smelter plans to make 50000 t of aluminium a year. Using the rounded illustrative ratio (5 t bauxite → 2 t alumina → 1 t aluminium), how much alumina and bauxite does it need? Why should it be close to a power station?

**Step 1.** Alumina $= 50000 \times 2 = 100000$ t.

**Step 2.** Bauxite $= 50000 \times 5 = 250000$ t.

**Step 3. Location.** Smelting by electrolysis needs very large amounts of electricity, so a smelter is best placed near cheap hydel or thermal power, while the refinery stays near the bulky bauxite.

visual.alt: Flow of illustrative tonnages from bauxite to alumina to aluminium for one smelter

slides.narration: To make fifty thousand tonnes of aluminium, the smelter needs twice as much alumina, one hundred thousand tonnes, which comes from five times as much bauxite, two hundred and fifty thousand tonnes. The refinery is placed near the mines, because bauxite is bulky. The smelter is placed near a cheap supply of electricity, because splitting alumina into aluminium uses enormous amounts of power.

slides.heading: Summary: Part 2
bullets: Copper: excellent conductor, ductile; wires, motors, electronics, utensils; alloys brass (with zinc) and bronze (with tin).
Copper areas: Madhya Pradesh (Malanjkhand, Balaghat), Rajasthan (Khetri, Jhunjhunu), Jharkhand (Singhbhum); low-grade ores, so India imports copper.
Bauxite: ore of aluminium; aluminium is light, strong, rust-free — aircraft, power cables, utensils, packaging.
Bauxite areas: Odisha (Koraput, Kalahandi), Gujarat (Jamnagar, Kutch), Jharkhand (Lohardaga), Chhattisgarh, Maharashtra. Bauxite → alumina (refinery) → aluminium (smelter, cheap power).

slides.narration: Let us sum up Part 2. Copper conducts electricity very well and is used for wires, motors and electronics, and in brass and bronze. It is mined at Malanjkhand, Khetri and in Singhbhum. Bauxite is the ore of aluminium, a light, strong metal used for aircraft, power lines and utensils. Odisha and Gujarat lead in bauxite, and smelters are built near cheap electricity.

Remember the chain: bauxite → alumina → aluminium.
Brass is copper + zinc; bronze is copper + tin.

notes.title: Mineral Resources — Notes

sections.heading: 1. Minerals, ores and grade
sections.body_md:
- **Mineral:** natural substance with a definite chemical composition.
- **Ore:** rock from which a metal can be extracted profitably.
- **Grade:** share of metal in an ore; high grade → more metal, less waste.
- **Ferrous** (iron ore, manganese) and **non-ferrous** (copper, bauxite) metallic minerals.
- Metal in an ore = grade ÷ 100 × tonnes of ore.

key_terms.definition_md: A mineral or rock from which a metal can be extracted profitably.
The proportion of metal contained in an ore.

visual.alt: Table classifying the four minerals as ferrous or non-ferrous

sections.heading: 2. Iron ore: types and uses
sections.body_md:
- **Magnetite:** black, magnetic; richest (up to about 70% iron).
- **Hematite:** reddish; about 60–70% iron; most mined in India.
- **Limonite:** yellowish-brown, hydrated; lower grade (about 35–50%).
- **Siderite:** iron carbonate; many impurities; low grade.
- **Uses:** smelted with coke and limestone in a blast furnace → pig iron → steel for railways, bridges, ships, buildings, machinery, vehicles, tools, utensils.
- Grade values are approximate and vary between deposits.

key_terms.definition_md: A reddish iron ore with a high iron content; the ore most mined in India.
A black, magnetic iron ore with the highest iron content.

visual.alt: Table of the four iron ores with colour and grade

sections.heading: 3. Iron ore: distribution
sections.body_md:
- **Leading states (as of the early 2020s): Odisha and Chhattisgarh**; also Karnataka and Jharkhand.
- **Odisha:** Keonjhar (Joda, Barbil), Sundargarh (Bonai), Mayurbhanj (Gorumahisani, Badampahar, Sulaipat).
- **Chhattisgarh:** Bailadila range (Dantewada); Dalli-Rajhara (supplies Bhilai).
- **Jharkhand:** Noamundi, Gua (Singhbhum).
- **Karnataka:** Bellary–Hospet (Sandur).
- Mostly **open-cast** mining of thick surface deposits on hill tops.
- Steel plants are built near the mines because iron ore is heavy and bulky (Bhilai, Rourkela).

key_terms.definition_md: Mining from an open pit after removing the overburden, used where the ore lies near the surface.

visual.alt: Table of iron-ore states and a mining area in each

sections.heading: 4. Manganese
sections.body_md:
- **Uses:** steel making (ferro-manganese hardens steel and removes impurities); dry-cell batteries; bleaching powder; insecticides; paints; glass and ceramics.
- **Leading states (as of the early 2020s):** Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Odisha; also Karnataka.
- **Areas:** Balaghat and Chhindwara (Madhya Pradesh); Nagpur and Bhandara (Maharashtra); Keonjhar, Sundargarh, Koraput (Odisha); Sandur (Karnataka).

key_terms.definition_md: An alloy of iron and manganese used to harden steel and remove impurities.

visual.alt: Table of manganese states and areas

sections.heading: 5. Copper
sections.body_md:
- **Properties:** excellent conductor of electricity and heat; ductile; malleable; resists corrosion.
- **Uses:** electrical cables and wires, motors, transformers, generators, electronics, utensils, coins; alloys **brass** (copper + zinc) and **bronze** (copper + tin).
- **Leading states (as of the early 2020s):** Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan; also Jharkhand.
- **Areas:** Malanjkhand (Balaghat, Madhya Pradesh); Khetri–Singhana (Jhunjhunu, Rajasthan), Alwar; Singhbhum belt — Ghatsila, Mosabani, Rakha (Jharkhand).
- Reserves are limited and low grade, so India imports much copper.

key_terms.definition_md: An alloy of copper and zinc.
An alloy of copper and tin.

visual.alt: Table of copper states and areas

sections.heading: 6. Bauxite
sections.body_md:
- **Bauxite:** ore of aluminium (hydrated aluminium oxide), found in laterite areas.
- **Aluminium:** light, strong, good conductor, does not rust; aircraft, vehicles, overhead cables, utensils, foil and cans, window frames. Bauxite also used for cement, abrasives, refractories.
- **Process:** bauxite → **alumina** (refinery, e.g. Damanjodi) → **aluminium** (smelter, e.g. Angul, Hirakud, Renukoot); smelting needs huge amounts of electricity. Rounded ratio about 5 : 2 : 1 by mass.
- **Leading states (as of the early 2020s):** Odisha and Gujarat; also Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh.
- **Areas:** Koraput (Panchpatmali), Kalahandi (Odisha); Jamnagar, Kutch, Bhavnagar (Gujarat); Lohardaga (Jharkhand); Mainpat, Amarkantak (Chhattisgarh); Kolhapur, Ratnagiri (Maharashtra).

key_terms.definition_md: Aluminium oxide, the white powder refined from bauxite and smelted into aluminium.
A plant where alumina is turned into aluminium by electrolysis.

visual.alt: Table of bauxite states and areas

notes.exam_tips_md:
**Common mistakes**
- Calling limonite the richest iron ore (it is magnetite).
- Placing Bailadila in Odisha or Khetri in Madhya Pradesh.
- Writing bronze as copper + zinc (that is brass).
- Saying bauxite is smelted directly (it is first refined to alumina).

**How marks are usually awarded**
- Uses: one mark per specific use (with the property where asked).
- Distribution: state plus a named mining area for each mark.
- Ore calculations: grade ÷ 100 × tonnes, with the unit.

questions.stem_md: A geologist finds a yellowish-brown, earthy iron ore of fairly low grade that contains water in its structure. It is most likely:
questions.solution_md: Yellow-brown, hydrated and of lower grade — option (b).

questions.stem_md: Most of the iron ore mined in Odisha and Chhattisgarh for Indian steel plants is reddish and has a high iron content. This ore is:
questions.solution_md: Option (c).

questions.stem_md: Joda and Barbil are iron-ore mining centres in:
questions.solution_md: Option (b).

questions.stem_md: The Bhilai steel plant obtains much of its iron ore from the nearby mines of:
questions.solution_md: Dalli-Rajhara in Chhattisgarh lies close to Bhilai — option (c).

questions.stem_md: Which two states were the leading producers of iron ore in India in the early 2020s?
questions.solution_md: Option (a).

questions.stem_md: A steel company wants to buy high-grade hematite from a single large deposit. Which source would be most suitable?

options.text_md: The Khetri belt in Jhunjhunu, Rajasthan
The Bailadila range in Dantewada, Chhattisgarh

questions.solution_md: Bailadila is famous for very high-grade hematite; the others are copper or bauxite areas — option (d).

questions.stem_md: Steel plants such as Rourkela and Bhilai were built close to iron-ore mines mainly because:

options.text_md: steel can be made only inside forests
iron ore is heavy and bulky, so carrying it long distances is costly
iron ore spoils quickly in storage
mines are always next to sea ports

questions.solution_md: Weight and bulk of the raw material favour locations near the ore — option (b).

questions.stem_md: Iron ore in the Bailadila and Keonjhar hills is mined mainly by open-cast methods because:

options.text_md: the ore lies thousands of metres below the surface
the ore is found dissolved in sea water
the ore lies in thick deposits close to the surface

questions.solution_md: Near-surface deposits can be dug from open pits after removing the overburden — option (d).

questions.stem_md: Why would a steel plant prefer high-grade hematite to a low-grade siderite ore?

options.text_md: Siderite cannot be found anywhere in the world
It gives more iron per tonne, so less rock has to be mined, carried and smelted

questions.solution_md: Higher grade means less waste per tonne of iron — option (c).

questions.stem_md:
**Assertion (A):** Most of the iron ore mined in India is hematite.

**Reason (R):** India has large deposits of high-grade hematite in Odisha, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand and Karnataka.

Choose the correct option.

options.text_md: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

questions.solution_md: Both are true, and the large hematite deposits explain why it dominates mining — option (a).

questions.stem_md:
**Assertion (A):** Magnetite has the highest iron content of the iron ores.

**Reason (R):** Magnetite is a carbonate of iron.

Choose the correct option.

options.text_md: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

questions.solution_md: A is true; R is false: magnetite is an oxide of iron; siderite is the carbonate — option (c).

questions.stem_md: True or false? A plant would need to mine less rock to obtain 100 tonnes of iron from limonite than from magnetite.
questions.solution_md: False: limonite has a lower iron content, so more rock is needed.

questions.stem_md: The black iron ore that is attracted by a magnet is called ___.
questions.solution_md: **Magnetite**.

questions.stem_md: Iron ore is smelted with coke and limestone in a ___ furnace to make pig iron.
questions.solution_md: **Blast** furnace.

questions.stem_md: Name one iron-ore mining area in Chhattisgarh.
questions.solution_md: Bailadila.

questions.stem_md: Name the four types of iron ore in order of decreasing iron content, and state which of them is mined most in India.

answer.model_answer_md: Magnetite, hematite, limonite, siderite. Hematite is mined most in India.

questions.solution_md: Order; hematite.

questions.stem_md: Why is iron ore often called the backbone of industrial development? Give two reasons.

answer.model_answer_md: Iron ore is the raw material for iron and steel, which almost every other industry needs for its machines, tools, buildings and transport. Steel is also needed for railways, bridges, ships, vehicles and defence equipment, so the growth of a nation’s economy depends on it.

questions.solution_md: Raw material for steel; steel needed by all sectors.

questions.stem_md: Name the two leading iron-ore producing states of India and one mining area in each.

answer.model_answer_md: Odisha — Keonjhar (Joda, Barbil), Sundargarh or Mayurbhanj (Gorumahisani). Chhattisgarh — Bailadila or Dalli-Rajhara.

questions.solution_md: Odisha and Chhattisgarh with areas.

questions.stem_md: Give three reasons why the region where Odisha, Jharkhand and Chhattisgarh meet has several large steel plants.

answer.model_answer_md: Rich deposits of high-grade hematite lie in Keonjhar, Sundargarh, Singhbhum and Chhattisgarh, and iron ore is heavy, so plants are built near it. Coking coal from the Jharkhand fields, and limestone, dolomite and manganese, are found in the same region. A dense railway network links mines, coalfields and plants, and rivers provide water for cooling.

questions.solution_md: Iron ore; other raw materials; transport and water.

questions.stem_md: An illustrative hematite deposit has ore containing 65% iron. How many tonnes of iron are contained in 2400 t of this ore?
How many tonnes of limonite ore containing 45% iron (illustrative) must be smelted to obtain 900 t of iron?
Manganese is essential to the steel industry mainly because:

options.text_md: as ferro-manganese it hardens steel and removes impurities
it is the main fuel of blast furnaces
it gives steel a red colour

questions.solution_md: Option (a).

questions.stem_md: Apart from steel making, manganese is used in making:

options.text_md: dry-cell batteries, bleaching powder and paints

questions.solution_md: Option (b).

questions.stem_md: Balaghat and Chhindwara are important manganese-mining districts of:
questions.solution_md: Option (d).

questions.stem_md: A battery factory near Nagpur buys manganese ore from mines less than a hundred kilometres away. These mines are most likely in:
questions.solution_md: Nagpur and Bhandara districts have manganese mines — option (d).

questions.stem_md:
**Assertion (A):** Odisha produces both iron ore and manganese.

**Reason (R):** Manganese is used in making dry-cell batteries.

Choose the correct option.

options.text_md: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

questions.solution_md: Both are true, but a use of manganese does not explain where the two minerals occur — option (b).

questions.stem_md: True or false? Manganese is grouped with the ferrous minerals because it is used mainly with iron in making steel.
questions.solution_md: True.

questions.stem_md: An alloy of iron and manganese used in steel making is called ___.
questions.solution_md: **Ferro-manganese**.

questions.stem_md: State two uses of manganese, one of which is in the steel industry.

answer.model_answer_md: It is made into ferro-manganese, which hardens steel and removes impurities such as sulphur and oxygen. It is also used to make dry-cell batteries (or bleaching powder, paints, insecticides).

questions.solution_md: Steel hardening; batteries or bleaching powder.

questions.stem_md: Name two leading manganese-producing states and one mining area in each. Why is it useful to steel plants that manganese is often found near iron-ore regions?

answer.model_answer_md: Madhya Pradesh — Balaghat or Chhindwara; Maharashtra — Nagpur or Bhandara (Odisha — Keonjhar or Sundargarh is also accepted). Every steel plant needs manganese to harden steel and remove impurities; when it is mined in the same region as iron ore, as in Odisha, both raw materials can be brought cheaply over short distances.

questions.solution_md: Two states with areas; nearness cuts transport cost.

questions.stem_md: Which alloy is made by mixing copper with zinc?
questions.solution_md: Option (b).

questions.stem_md: Craftsmen in Thanjavur cast temple statues from an alloy of copper and tin. This alloy is:
questions.solution_md: Copper + tin = bronze — option (a).

questions.stem_md: Malanjkhand, a large open-cast copper mine, lies in:
questions.solution_md: Option (a).

questions.stem_md: The Khetri copper complex is located in:
questions.solution_md: Khetri is in Jhunjhunu district, Rajasthan — option (a).

questions.stem_md: India imports a large share of the copper it uses. The main reason is that:

options.text_md: copper has no use in India
its copper ores are limited and mostly of low grade, while demand from power and electronics is high
Indian factories cannot use metal wires
India’s copper ores are too pure to process

questions.solution_md: Small, low-grade reserves cannot meet rising demand — option (b).

questions.stem_md: A state launches a large programme to wire every village for electricity and to set up electric-motor workshops. The demand for which mineral is most likely to rise?
questions.solution_md: Wiring and motors use copper — option (a).

questions.stem_md:
**Assertion (A):** Copper is widely used for electrical wiring.

**Reason (R):** Copper is an excellent conductor of electricity and can be drawn into thin wires.

Choose the correct option.

options.text_md: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

questions.solution_md: Both are true, and R explains A — option (a).

questions.stem_md: True or false? Bronze is an alloy of copper and tin.
questions.solution_md: True.

questions.stem_md: The Malanjkhand copper mine is in the ___ district of Madhya Pradesh.
questions.solution_md: **Balaghat**.

questions.stem_md: Name the copper-mining belt of Jharkhand.
questions.solution_md: Singhbhum.

questions.stem_md: State two uses of copper and the property of copper on which each depends.

answer.model_answer_md: Electrical wires and cables — copper is an excellent conductor of electricity and is ductile. Cooking vessels and heat exchangers — it conducts heat well and resists corrosion (alloys such as brass and bronze are also accepted with a property).

questions.solution_md: Wires (conductivity); utensils (heat conduction).

questions.stem_md: A cable manufacturer in Indore wants to buy copper mined in India. Name two states, with one mining area in each, from which it could obtain copper, and explain why it may still have to import part of its copper.

answer.model_answer_md: Madhya Pradesh — Malanjkhand in Balaghat district (close to Indore); Rajasthan — Khetri–Singhana in Jhunjhunu district (Jharkhand — Ghatsila or Mosabani in Singhbhum is also accepted). India’s copper reserves are small and mostly of low grade, so domestic output falls well short of the demand from cable, power and electronics makers, and the rest has to be imported.

questions.solution_md: Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan with areas; limited, low-grade reserves.

questions.stem_md: An illustrative copper ore contains 1.2% copper. How many tonnes of copper can be obtained from 25000 t of ore?
With the same illustrative grade (1.2% copper), how many tonnes of ore must be mined to obtain 900 t of copper?
Before it is smelted into aluminium, bauxite is first refined into:
questions.solution_md: Bauxite → alumina → aluminium — option (d).

questions.stem_md: Aluminium rather than steel is used for most of the body of an aircraft mainly because aluminium is:

options.text_md: light yet strong, and does not rust

questions.solution_md: Option (a).

questions.stem_md: Long overhead high-voltage transmission lines often use aluminium conductors rather than copper. Which reason best explains this?

options.text_md: Aluminium conducts electricity better than any other metal
Aluminium is much lighter and cheaper, while still conducting electricity well
Copper cannot be drawn into wires
Aluminium is heavier, so the lines sag less

questions.solution_md: Lightness and cost matter for long spans on towers — option (b).

questions.stem_md: Which two states were the leading producers of bauxite in India in the early 2020s?
questions.solution_md: Option (c).

questions.stem_md: Aluminium smelters such as those at Renukoot and Hirakud are located close to sources of cheap electricity because:

options.text_md: bauxite is mined only near power stations
aluminium must be stored in water
turning alumina into aluminium uses very large amounts of electricity
electricity makes bauxite lighter to carry

questions.solution_md: Smelting by electrolysis is power-hungry — option (c).

questions.stem_md: Which group lists only bauxite-producing areas?
questions.solution_md: The other groups are copper, manganese and iron-ore areas — option (d).

questions.stem_md: An alumina refinery, such as the one at Damanjodi in Odisha, is usually built close to the bauxite mines because:

options.text_md: alumina cannot be transported at all
bauxite is bulky and loses much of its weight when refined, so it is cheaper to refine it near the mine

questions.solution_md: A weight-losing raw material is processed near its source — option (c).

questions.stem_md:
**Assertion (A):** Bauxite is used mainly as a fuel in thermal power stations.

**Reason (R):** Bauxite is the main ore of aluminium.

Choose the correct option.

options.text_md: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

questions.solution_md: A is false: bauxite is not a fuel; R is true — option (d).

questions.stem_md:
**Assertion (A):** An aluminium smelter was set up at Hirakud in Odisha.

**Reason (R):** The Hirakud dam supplies hydroelectricity, and smelting aluminium needs large amounts of power.

Choose the correct option.

options.text_md: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

questions.solution_md: Both are true, and the cheap power explains the location — option (a).

questions.stem_md: True or false? Bauxite is smelted directly into aluminium without any intermediate product.
questions.solution_md: False: it is first refined into alumina, which is then smelted.

questions.stem_md: True or false? Smelting alumina into aluminium needs only a little electricity, so smelters can be built anywhere.
questions.solution_md: False: smelting by electrolysis needs very large amounts of electricity, so smelters are sited near cheap power.

questions.stem_md: The white powder obtained by refining bauxite, which is then smelted into aluminium, is called ___.
questions.solution_md: **Alumina**.

questions.stem_md: State two uses of aluminium and link each to a property of the metal.

answer.model_answer_md: Aircraft and vehicle bodies — it is light yet strong. Overhead power cables — it conducts electricity well and is light (also utensils, as it conducts heat and does not rust; foil and cans, as it rolls thin).

questions.solution_md: Two uses with properties.

questions.stem_md: In Odisha, alumina is made at Damanjodi near the Koraput bauxite mines, while aluminium is smelted at Angul, near large power stations. Explain why the two stages are located differently.

answer.model_answer_md: Bauxite is bulky and about half its weight is lost when it is refined into alumina, so refining near the mines (Damanjodi near Koraput) avoids carrying waste. Alumina is much lighter and more valuable per tonne, so it can bear the cost of transport to the smelter. Smelting alumina into aluminium by electrolysis needs enormous amounts of electricity, so the smelter is placed where cheap power is available, as at Angul with its thermal power stations.

questions.solution_md: Weight loss favours the mine; power demand favours the power source.

questions.stem_md: Using the rounded illustrative ratio of 5 t of bauxite for every 1 t of aluminium, how many tonnes of bauxite are needed to make 30000 t of aluminium?
questions.solution_md: Bauxite $= 30000 \times 5 = 150000$ t.

questions.stem_md: An imagined company’s four bauxite mines produce (lakh tonnes a year, illustrative): Mine A 12, Mine B 8, Mine C 3, Mine D 2. What percentage of the company’s output comes from Mine A?
Match each mineral in Column A with a mining area in Column B.
questions.solution_md: Iron ore → Noamundi; manganese → Bhandara; copper → Khetri; bauxite → Lohardaga.

questions.stem_md: Match each mineral in Column A with a typical use in Column B.
questions.solution_md: Iron ore → rails; manganese → batteries; copper → wiring; bauxite → aircraft.

questions.stem_md:
(a) Name the four types of iron ore. Which of them is the richest? [2]

(b) State two uses of iron. [2]

(c) Name the two leading iron-ore producing states of India and two mining areas in each. [3]

(d) Explain three reasons why steel plants such as Bhilai and Rourkela are located near iron-ore mines. [3]

answer.model_answer_md:
(a) Magnetite, hematite, limonite and siderite; magnetite is the richest.

(b) Making steel for railways, bridges and buildings; machinery, vehicles, tools and utensils (also ships and defence equipment).

(c) Odisha — Keonjhar (Joda, Barbil), Sundargarh (Bonai) or Mayurbhanj (Gorumahisani). Chhattisgarh — Bailadila (Dantewada) and Dalli-Rajhara.

(d) Iron ore is heavy and bulky, so carrying it long distances raises costs; coking coal, limestone, dolomite and manganese are found in the same region; railways link the mines to the plants, and nearby rivers supply water.

questions.solution_md: Types; uses; states and areas; location reasons.

questions.stem_md:
(a) State two uses of manganese. [2]

(b) Name two leading manganese-producing states and one mining area in each. [2]

(c) Using illustrative grades of 65% iron for hematite and 45% for limonite, calculate the iron contained in 3000 t of each ore and the difference. [3]

(d) Using your answer to (c), explain why steel plants prefer high-grade ore, and why they also need manganese. [3]

answer.model_answer_md:
(a) Making ferro-manganese, which hardens steel and removes impurities; dry-cell batteries (also bleaching powder, paints, insecticides).

(b) Madhya Pradesh — Balaghat or Chhindwara; Maharashtra — Nagpur or Bhandara (Odisha — Keonjhar also accepted).

(c) Hematite: $\frac{65}{100} \times 3000 = 1950$ t; limonite: $\frac{45}{100} \times 3000 = 1350$ t; difference $= 1950 - 1350 = 600$ t.

(d) The same tonnage of hematite yields 600 t more iron, so less rock must be mined, carried and smelted for each tonne of steel, saving fuel and transport and producing less waste. Manganese is still needed because, as ferro-manganese, it hardens the steel and removes impurities such as sulphur and oxygen.

questions.solution_md: Uses; states; 1950 t, 1350 t, difference 600 t; grade and manganese.

questions.stem_md:
(a) State two uses of copper. [2]

(b) What are brass and bronze? [2]

(c) Name the two leading copper-producing states and one mining area in each, and a copper belt of Jharkhand. [3]

(d) A mine works ore containing 1.2% copper (illustrative). Calculate the copper obtained from 60000 t of ore, and use your answer to explain why India imports much of its copper. [3]

answer.model_answer_md:
(a) Electrical wires and cables; motors, transformers and electronics (also utensils, coins).

(b) Brass is an alloy of copper and zinc; bronze is an alloy of copper and tin.

(c) Madhya Pradesh — Malanjkhand (Balaghat); Rajasthan — Khetri–Singhana (Jhunjhunu). Jharkhand — the Singhbhum belt (Ghatsila, Mosabani).

(d) Copper $= \frac{1.2}{100} \times 60000 = 720$ t. Almost all of the rock is waste, so production is costly; India’s reserves are small and of low grade, while demand for wiring, power equipment and electronics keeps rising, so the shortfall is met by imports.

questions.solution_md: Uses; alloys; areas; 720 t and imports.

questions.stem_md:
(a) State two uses of aluminium. [2]

(b) Name the two leading bauxite-producing states and one mining area in each. [2]

(c) Describe the stages by which bauxite is turned into aluminium, naming one place in Odisha for each stage. [3]

(d) Using the rounded illustrative ratio 5 : 2 : 1 (bauxite : alumina : aluminium), calculate the alumina and bauxite needed by a smelter making 40000 t of aluminium, and state why the smelter needs cheap power. [3]

answer.model_answer_md:
(a) Aircraft and vehicle bodies; overhead electric cables (also utensils, foil and cans, window frames).

(b) Odisha — Koraput (Panchpatmali) or Kalahandi; Gujarat — Jamnagar, Kutch or Bhavnagar.

(c) Bauxite is mined (Panchpatmali, Koraput); it is refined into alumina at a refinery (Damanjodi); alumina is smelted by electrolysis into aluminium at a smelter (Angul or Hirakud).

(d) Alumina $= 40000 \times 2 = 80000$ t; bauxite $= 40000 \times 5 = 200000$ t. Smelting alumina into aluminium uses very large amounts of electricity, so cheap power keeps costs down.

questions.solution_md: Uses; states; stages; 80000 t alumina, 200000 t bauxite.

questions.stem_md:
(a) Classify iron ore, manganese, copper and bauxite as ferrous or non-ferrous minerals. [2]

(b) Name the mineral mined at each of: Malanjkhand, Koraput, Noamundi and Balaghat–Chhindwara. [2]

(c) An imagined company’s four bauxite mines produce (lakh tonnes a year, illustrative): Mine A 12, Mine B 8, Mine C 3, Mine D 2. Calculate the share of Mine A and the combined share of Mines C and D in the total output. [3]

(d) Explain three reasons why Odisha has become a major centre of mineral-based industries such as steel and aluminium. [3]

answer.model_answer_md:
(a) Ferrous: iron ore and manganese. Non-ferrous: copper and bauxite.

(b) Malanjkhand — copper; Koraput — bauxite; Noamundi — iron ore; Balaghat–Chhindwara — manganese.

(c) Total $= 12 + 8 + 3 + 2 = 25$ lakh tonnes. Mine A $= \frac{12}{25} \times 100 = 48$%; Mines C and D $= \frac{3 + 2}{25} \times 100 = 20$%.

(d) Odisha has rich deposits of iron ore (Keonjhar, Sundargarh), manganese and bauxite (Koraput) close together; coal from its own Talcher and Ib valley fields and from Jharkhand provides power and coke; hydel and thermal power (Hirakud, Angul), railways and the port of Paradip support heavy industry and exports.

questions.solution_md: Ferrous and non-ferrous; four areas; 48% and 20%; reasons for Odisha.
